html:
In 332 BCE Alexander the Great besieged Tyre, the richest Phoenician city, which stood on an island off the coast of Lebanon. The siege lasted about seven months.

Tyre refused to let Alexander into its temple. Since he had no fleet strong enough, he built a causeway out across the sea to the island, while the Tyrians attacked the work with fire ships. When ships from other Phoenician cities joined him, he broke the walls. Thousands were killed, and many of the survivors were sold as slaves.

The causeway silted up over the centuries, and Tyre is now joined to the mainland. The fall of Tyre ended the independence of the Phoenician cities, which became part of the Greek world of Alexander's conquests.
